receipt.scope: Finite token-level causal measurement on reused development. No new program result, semantic meaning, coding improvement or novelty.

full_state_control.interpretation: Descriptive scale, not mediation or circuit fraction.

interpretation.conclusion: The fixed small group has a controlled finite causal contribution to comparator-token scores in this assay. Opposite donors change the margin substantially more than same-policy donors and both magnitude-matched random groups. Clean zeroing also shifts scores, and cuts reduce the engineered full-opposite margin. These score effects are insufficient to switch any of the thirteen programs in the closed parent study.
interpretation.gradient_interpretation: The selected64 finite means approximately match the archived first-order sums on the same eight discovery cases. This does not establish a universal approximation bound or a precision-specific mechanism. All six groups and all four strata remain reported.
interpretation.limits: Reused, dependent development cases; response-derived current decision; semantic versus lexical role unresolved; no individual neuron meaning, program-level necessity/sufficiency, deployable trigger, novelty or coding improvement. The other-five cohort has one filter and four predicates, all under the second wording.
interpretation.next_question: Consider a separately frozen answer-independent runtime trigger for the already prescribed gain of two and fixed groups on new error-bearing complete coding tasks. This would be development, not confirmation. Do not assume that reinforcing a chosen operator improves correctness or choose a new dose or coordinate from N24.
